message.abstract: <jats:p><jats:italic><jats:bold>Purpose</jats:bold>:</jats:italic> Despite the increasing body of literature on badminton, no data exist concerning the energy cost of badminton movement, known as “footwork.” This study introduces a novel experimental approach to assessing the energy cost of footwork by applying established metabolic measurement techniques to badminton-specific movement patterns for the first time. In addition, it aims to verify whether differences exist between 2 different movement combinations. <jats:italic><jats:bold>Methods</jats:bold>:</jats:italic> Seven male and 7 female badminton athletes (age 19 [4] y; body mass 64.9 [8.4] kg; height 1.72 [0.08] m; <jats:inline-formula/> 55.5 [10.3] mL·kg<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>·min<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>) completed 2 sets of 12 repetitions of 4 all-out preplanned footwork exercises with 30 seconds of passive recovery, using 2 types of steps (side step and running step). During exercises, respiratory data, blood lactate concentration, and net energy cost (C<jats:sub>netFW</jats:sub>, J·kg<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>·m<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>) were determined, along with total exercise duration and average speed. <jats:italic><jats:bold>Results</jats:bold>:</jats:italic> C<jats:sub>netFW</jats:sub> was 19.59 (4.46) for side step and 20.38 (4.52) J·kg<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>·m<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> for running step. No significant differences in metabolic data, total exercise duration, or average speed were observed (<jats:italic>P</jats:italic> < .05). C<jats:sub>netFW</jats:sub> data showed a positive linear correlation between energy cost and footwork speed (<jats:italic>r</jats:italic> = .62; <jats:italic>r</jats:italic><jats:sup>2</jats:sup> = .39; <jats:italic>P</jats:italic> = .0009). <jats:italic><jats:bold>Conclusions</jats:bold>:</jats:italic> C<jats:sub>netFW</jats:sub> increases with speed, but there is no significant difference between the 2 types of footwork. Players and coaches can choose the most appropriate step combinations based on individual characteristics and specific game requirements.</jats:p>
title: Energy Cost of Badminton Footwork: A Novel Experimental Approach
